ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As the figure shows, $AD$ is the median of $\triangle ABC$, and $E$ is a point on $AD$ with $DE=2AE$. The extension of $CE$ intersects $AB$ at point $F$. If $AF=1.6\text{cm}$, then what is the length of $AB$ in $\text{cm}$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Let DM be drawn parallel to CF and intersect AB at M,\\
since $DM\parallel CF$,\\
then $\frac{BD}{DC}=\frac{BM}{MF}$,\\
since AD is the median of $\triangle ABC$,\\
then D is the midpoint of BC,\\
thus BD=DC,\\
thus $\frac{BD}{DC}=\frac{BM}{MF}=1$,\\
thus BM=MF,\\
since EF$\parallel$MD,\\
then $\triangle AFE\sim \triangle AMD$,\\
also since DE=2AE,\\
then $\frac{AF}{AM}=\frac{AE}{AD}=\frac{AE}{DE+AE}=\frac{AE}{2AE+AE}=\frac{1}{3}$,\\
thus AM=3AF,\\
since AM=AF+MF=3AF,\\
then MF=2AF,\\
since BM=MF,\\
then BM=MF=2AF,\\
thus AB=AF+MF+BF=5AF,\\
since AF=1.6,\\
thus AB=$5\times 1.6$=\boxed{8},

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: In the figure, $AD$ is the median of $\triangle ABC$, and $E$ is a point on $AD$ with $DE=2AE$. The extension of $CE$ intersects $AB$ at point $F$. If $AF=1.6\text{ cm}$, what is the length of $AB$ in $\text{ cm}$?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the attached figure, A of triangle ABC is above, B is at the lower left, and C is at the lower right; point D is located on BC, and line segment AD is drawn; point E is located on AD; the straight line starting from C and passing through E, after being extended, intersects AB at F, and F is on AB. Reasoning: From the meaning of the problem, AD is the median of triangle ABC, so BD=DC. Using the mass points method, let m_B=m_C=1, then the mass at D is m_D=1+1=2. Also DE=2AE, so AE:ED=1:2. On AD, AE:ED=m_D:m_A, therefore 1:2=2:m_A, giving m_A=4. Since C, E, F are collinear and F is on AB, on AB the mass points give AF:FB=m_B:m_A=1:4, so AF accounts for 1/(1+4)=1/5 of AB. It is known that AF=1.6 cm, therefore AB=5×1.6=8 cm.
